correctness.rationale: The arbitrary-slice lower bound is complete. Urysohn localization near a non-isolated point forces radius at least \(1+\beta(f)\). For each active isolated point, sign alignment and a one-coordinate perturbation yield the sharp atomic inequality \(a_t(R+1-|f(t)|)\ge\alpha\); combining it with the slice defect gives every finite-subsum active constraint and hence \(\Phi_f(R)\le1\). Conversely, above any feasible radius the active isolated set is finite, reciprocal-width weights define a norm-one atomic functional, and its slice separates all coordinate-bad faces. Letting the auxiliary radius decrease proves equality. Infinite sums are handled as suprema of finite subsums, and the boundary is reached by approximation. The bundled finite checker was inspected only as a verification of the finite separation algebra, not as proof of the compact-Hausdorff localization.

final_claim: For every infinite compact Hausdorff space K and real f in the unit ball of C(K), the pointwise Delta constant is the least r in [1,2] satisfying both r at least 1 plus the maximum of |f| on the non-isolated core and the isolated-point active sum \(\sum_{|f(t)|>r-1}(1-|f(t)|)/(r+1-|f(t)|)\le1\); the convergent-sequence specialization and mixed isolated-peak examples follow.
